turns: I walk down to the landing and look around.
I greet the ferryman and ask what a crossing costs.
I haggle with him over the price.
I wander over to the woman at the firepit and ask what she is cooking.
I offer to buy one of her eels.
I sit by the fire and eat in silence, watching the river.
I ask her why she is waiting to cross.
I go back to the ferryman and ask about the pale, silent stretch of water.
I ask the ferryman for his real name, and I wait until he answers.
I tell them both I need to reach the far bank before dark.
I step onto the raft and take hold of the rope.
Halfway across, I hear the rope start to fray.
I shout for the ferryman to help me hold the rope.
I ask the woman whether she has made this crossing before.
I look back at the landing as we pull across.
